For references to the use of the vaso- pressin analogue, desmopressin, in nocturnal enuresis, see p.2187. Shock. Argipressin has been reported to have beneficial vaso- pressor effects in the management of shock (p.1183) due to va- sodilatation. It has been given by continuous intravenous infu- sion at a dose of about 2 to 6 units/hour as supplemental therapy in patients who could not be adequately managed with conven- tional vasopressor therapy.1,2 In a retrospective study3 vaso- pressin given with or without catecholamines for haemodynamic support of shock did not increase the incidence of venous throm- boembolism compared with catecholamines given alone. Further reports4,5 of the benefit of vasopressin in septic shock suggest that it may be of value in reducing doses of catecholamine vaso- pressors. 1. Dünser MW, et al.
